transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Everyone keeps saying I’m way too thin and sick, but I honestly don’t see what the big deal is about my weight right now. My family and coworkers are really making a mountain out of a molehill, so I'm basically just here because they insisted I get checked out.
When you look in the mirror, how do you see your body? Do you feel like you're underweight, normal, or overweight?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as dangerously thin at all—I just see a guy who looks fit and maybe a little tired from work. Staying lean is the one thing that makes me feel like I'm doing something right in my life, and I'm terrified that if my weight creeps up even a little, I'll become that sloppy, out-of-shape guy my ex used to nag about. Everyone else is really just making a mountain out of a molehill.
How do you feel about your current eating habits—do you restrict food, count calories closely, or avoid certain foods even if you're hungry?

Most days I just have a coffee in the morning, maybe a banana or half a sandwich at work, and soup or salad at night because I don't want to feel heavy or stuffed. I avoid heavy foods like pizza or desserts because even thinking about eating them makes me feel panicky, like my stomach is going to blow up overnight.
If your weight dropped even lower, would you still feel like you need to lose more, or would you start to worry about being too thin?

I don't think I would worry about it at all, to be honest. I actually kind of like seeing the numbers on the scale keep dropping, and I often think I could go a bit lower and still be perfectly fine. I really feel like everyone else is just overreacting to where I'm at right now.
